accept: secundum atrial septal defect with right heart volume overload

findings: Right bundle branch block with rSR pattern in lead V1
Right axis deviation with right ventricular hypertrophy

echoTasks.find: Dropout of the mid interatrial septum on subcostal views with left to right colour flow
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle with volume overload in the apical window
Dilated pulmonary trunk relative to the aorta with high pulmonary flow

auscultation.added: Mid diastolic rumble at the lower left sternal edge from high tricuspid flow
auscultation.murmur: Ejection systolic murmur grade 2 of 6 at the upper left sternal edge

exam.general: 6 year old girl, thin, pink, no distress, normal growth at the tenth centile
exam.other: Right ventricular heave, liver not enlarged, lungs clear
exam.precordium: Hyperdynamic right ventricle with a palpable pulmonary component

history.a: Recurrent cough with fast breathing since infancy, tires before peers in play
No blue spells, no squatting, no fainting
Two admissions for chest infection, treated fully
Parents healthy, no heart disease, one elder brother well
Attends school, immunised, referred from a school health camp

keyPoints: Refer to paediatric cardiology for device or surgical closure assessment, as large defects with right heart enlargement need closure
Treat intercurrent chest infections promptly and keep vaccines current
Counsel that most children are pink because the shunt is left to right at this stage
Plan activity as normal with infection vigilance while awaiting closure
Review yearly for pulmonary pressure rise if closure is deferred for any reason
management.model: Cardiology referral for closure with infection vigilance and growth tracking until repair

sources: ASE guideline on echocardiography in adult congenital heart disease, in own words
Indian Academy of Paediatrics guidance on congenital heart disease referral, in own words
stem: A 6 year old girl from Jaipur is referred from a school camp for recurrent chest infections and easy fatiguability. She is pink with a wide fixed split second sound and an ejection murmur from high pulmonary flow.
teaching: A wide fixed split second sound is the auscultatory signature of an atrial septal defect
Large means above 20 mm or a flow ratio above 2 with right heart enlargement
Subcostal bicaval imaging profiles the septum and rims for closure planning
Pink with recurrent infections and a hyperdynamic right ventricle completes the picture
title: Large atrial septal defect in a schoolgirl
